questions.question: Mahatma Gandhi famously said that 'religion can never be separated from politics'. What did he mean by 'religion' in this context?
options: Moral and ethical values drawn from all religions that should guide political governance
Strict legal imposition of orthodox Hindu rituals by the state
Banning all minority religious practices in public schools
Rule by religious priests and clergy instead of parliament
questions.explanation: Gandhiji used to say that religion can never be separated from politics. What he meant by religion was not any particular religion like Hinduism or Islam, but moral values that inform all religions. He believed that politics must be guided by ethics drawn from religion.

questions.question: Which of the following constitutional provisions reflects that India is a 'Secular State'?

Only religious scholars can contest parliamentary elections
There is no official religion for the Indian state, and Article 25 gives freedom to profess and practice any religion
The state funds religious temples exclusively from public taxes
